title: Ha Mim again, at the door of a twin surah.
subtitle: A pause before a surah of signs
then: Al-Jathiyah came right after Ad-Dukhan, and the two are so close they read like twins. It opens with the same letters, Ha and Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What follows is a surah about the signs all around us.
now: You saw Ha Mim at the start of the last surah too, and your eyes want to slide past. {idea}Treat each opening as a fresh knock at the door.{/idea} Something new is about to be said.
old: I have seen these letters before, so I can skip them.
new: Each time they appear, they ask me to stop and listen again.
try: Before you read this surah, take one slow breath and say bismillah with attention.

title: Sent down from the Mighty, the Wise.
subtitle: Who the Book comes from
then: The surah names its source straight away: the Book is {idea}a revelation from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise{/idea}. The Makkans had doubts about the Quran and about the Hereafter, and this surah answers them.
now: A letter arrives from someone very important and very wise. You would read it slowly, more than once. {idea}This Book's Sender is greater than any of them.{/idea}
old: The Quran is a good book among many.
new: The Quran comes from the Mighty, the Wise, so I read it that way.
try: Read one verse today as if it were a personal letter, and reread it once.

title: The heavens and earth are full of signs for believers.
subtitle: The first step: seeing with faith
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}directs His servants to contemplate His favours and His great power{/idea} in creating the heavens and earth and all kinds of creatures in them. He notes this is the first of three stages: signs for the believers.
now: You take a photo of the sunset for your story and forget it. {idea}The same sky, looked at with faith, is a message.{/idea} The view is the same. The seeing changes.
old: The sky is beautiful, and that is all it is.
new: The sky is a sign, and faith is what lets me read it.
try: Look up at the sky once today and say subhanallah before taking out your phone.

title: Your own body and every creature are signs.
subtitle: The second step: certainty
then: The signs come nearer: {idea}your own creation, and every moving creature spread on the earth{/idea}. Ibn Kathir lists angels, jinn, humans, animals, birds, insects and sea creatures. This time they are signs for {idea}people of certainty{/idea}, a higher stage.
now: You cut your finger and two days later it has healed. You never told it how. A cat stretches on the windowsill. {idea}You are surrounded by signs, and you are one of them.{/idea}
old: Signs are rare and dramatic.
new: My own body is a sign, healing and breathing without my help.
try: Put your hand on your chest for ten seconds today and thank Allah for your heartbeat.

title: Night and day, rain and winds, for those who think.
subtitle: The third step: understanding
then: Ibn Kathir says rain is called {reward}provision{/reward} because it produces all kinds of provision, reviving dry, dead earth. Winds turn north, south, east, west; some bring rain, some pollinate. He notes the verses rise {idea}from believers, to the certain, to those who understand{/idea}.
now: The weather app says rain tomorrow. You groan about the commute. {idea}Somewhere a dry field is waiting for exactly that rain.{/idea} Thinking about it turns a nuisance into a sign.
old: Weather is just something that happens to my plans.
new: Rain and wind are provision being sent, if I think about it.
try: Next time it rains, say the dua for rain or simply thank Allah for it.

title: After Allah's words, what will they believe?
subtitle: If not this, then what
then: Ibn Kathir says the verses {idea}contain the truth from the Truth{/idea}, meaning Allah. So if people do not believe Allah's verses, {trap}what speech after that will they believe in?{/trap}
now: You believe a stranger's video about diet, money and marriage within thirty seconds. You hold the Quran at arm's length. {trap}Notice whose words get your trust fastest.{/trap}
old: I should be sceptical of religious claims but open to others.
new: If I cannot trust His words, no other words deserve more trust.
try: Before you check your feed tomorrow morning, read one verse first.

title: Woe to every sinful liar.
subtitle: A heart shaped by lying
then: Ibn Kathir describes the sinful liar as one {trap}who lies in his speech, often swears{/trap}, and commits and utters sinful acts and words, then disbelieves in Allah's verses. Lying is listed first.
now: "I'm five minutes away" when you have not left. "I swear it was not me." {trap}Each small lie makes the truth a little easier to ignore.{/trap}
old: Little lies are just how everyday life works.
new: A habit of lying makes it harder to hear the truth when it comes.
try: Go one full day without a single small lie, even a polite one.

title: He hears the verses, then acts as if he did not.
subtitle: Hearing without letting it in
then: Ibn Kathir says this person hears the verses recited, {trap}yet persists in his disbelief, denial, pride and rebellion{/trap}, as if he never heard them. The sound reached his ears. Nothing reached his heart.
now: The imam's Friday reminder hits exactly your habit. You nod. By the car park you are back to normal. {trap}As if you had not heard.{/trap}
old: Hearing a reminder counts as taking it in.
new: A reminder I hear and do not act on is one I did not really hear.
try: Take one line from the last talk or reminder you heard and act on it today.

title: He learns a verse and turns it into a joke.
subtitle: Mocking what is sacred
then: Ibn Kathir says if this person {trap}learns anything from the Quran, he takes it as the subject of jest and ridicule{/trap}, and his punishment is humiliating, in return for mocking it. He notes the Prophet ﷺ forbade travelling with the Quran to enemy lands for fear it would be desecrated.
now: A meme in the group chat turns a verse into a punchline. Everyone sends laughing faces. {idea}You do not have to send one too.{/idea}
old: Laughing along with a religious joke is harmless.
new: Allah's words are not material for jokes, even small ones.
try: If you see a joke that mocks a verse, do not share it, and quietly say astaghfirullah.

title: What they earned and their allies will not help.
subtitle: Two kinds of backup that fail
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}their wealth and children will not avail them{/trap}, nor will the false gods they worshipped besides Allah. Everything they built up as protection gives nothing on that Day.
now: You keep a list in your head: the emergency fund, the cousin who is a lawyer, the friend with connections. {idea}All good things, and none of them is your real protector.{/idea}
old: With enough money and the right contacts, I am covered.
new: Money and contacts help here. Only Allah protects in the end.
try: When you check your savings this week, also say: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: This is guidance.
subtitle: Three words that sum up the Quran
then: After describing the liar and the mocker, the verse sums it up. Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is guidance{/idea} refers to the Quran. Those who disbelieve in their Lord's verses face {trap}a painful, severe torment{/trap}.
now: Your map app says: turn left. You can argue with it, but it knows the road. {idea}The Quran is guidance in that plain sense: directions.{/idea}
old: The Quran is mostly about restrictions.
new: The Quran is guidance, directions for getting where I need to go.
try: Read one passage today asking only: what direction is this giving me?

title: He made the sea carry your ships.
subtitle: Trade and travel as a gift to thank for
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}ordered the sea to carry ships{/idea}, so people could seek His bounty {reward}in commercial and business transactions{/reward}, and be thankful for provisions brought from distant lands.
now: The bananas in your kitchen crossed an ocean. Your phone was shipped in a container. {reward}Half of what you own floated to you.{/reward} The verse asks you to notice and thank.
old: Imported goods are just what shops sell.
new: The sea carrying my things to me is a favour from Allah.
try: Pick one item in your home that came from overseas and thank Allah for it.

title: All in the heavens and earth, put at your service.
subtitle: Everything is from Him alone
then: Ibn Kathir names {reward}the stars, the mountains, the seas, the rivers{/reward} and all that people use. Ibn Abbas said: {idea}everything is from Allah{/idea}, without rivals. It is a sign for people who think deeply.
now: You flick a switch and the lights come on. You open a tap. A GPS satellite finds you in seconds. {idea}All of it rests on a world that was made to serve you.{/idea}
old: The world just happens to be useful to us.
new: The world was put at my service, all of it from Him.
try: Spend one minute tonight thinking about one thing in nature that serves you every day.

title: Tell the believers to forgive those who harm them.
subtitle: Leaving the recompense to Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says in the beginning of Islam, believers were told to {idea}forgive and endure the harm{/idea} of the idolaters, so that their hearts might incline to Islam. Mujahid said those who hope not for Allah's Days are those who {trap}do not appreciate His favours{/trap}. Allah Himself will repay each.
now: A relative said something cruel at a family dinner. You replay it at night and plan your comeback. {idea}You can let it go and leave the account with Allah.{/idea}
old: If I forgive, they get away with it.
new: Forgiving does not erase their deed. It hands the account to Allah.
try: Think of one person who hurt you and say: Allah, I leave this with You.

title: Your good is for you, your harm is on you.
subtitle: Every deed comes back to its doer
then: Right after telling believers to forgive, the verse reminds them: {reward}good is for yourself{/reward}, {trap}evil is against yourself{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says all will return to Allah on the Day, when people and their actions are shown, and He will repay good with good and evil with evil.
now: You hold the door, stay late to help a colleague, and no one says thanks. It stings. {reward}That deed is filed under your name, not theirs.{/reward}
old: When my kindness goes unnoticed, it was wasted.
new: Every good I do is for me, noticed or not.
try: Do one kind thing today that no one will ever know was you.

title: Scripture, wisdom and prophethood were given before.
subtitle: The Children of Israel received great gifts
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah mentions the favours He gave the Children of Israel: {reward}revealing Divine Books, sending Messengers, and granting kingship{/reward}, good food and drink, and preference over the nations of their time.
now: You grew up with the Quran in the house, a masjid down the road, parents who prayed. {idea}Those are gifts many never had.{/idea} The question is what you are doing with them.
old: Having been raised with faith means I am on safe ground.
new: Being given much means I will be asked about much.
try: List three religious blessings you were given without asking, and thank Allah for each.

title: They split after knowledge came, out of rivalry.
subtitle: Division born of envy, not ignorance
then: Ibn Kathir says they were given clear proofs, {trap}yet they differed among themselves after the proof came, out of transgression against each other{/trap}. He says the verse is {idea}a warning to the Muslim Ummah as well{/idea}, not to take the same path.
now: Two masjid committees in the same town stop speaking. Both know the same verses. {trap}It is not knowledge they lack. It is the ego in the room.{/trap}
old: Arguments in a community are about who is right.
new: Many splits come from rivalry, after everyone already knew the truth.
try: Next time you disagree with a fellow Muslim, ask: is this about truth or about winning?

title: You are set on a clear way, so follow it.
subtitle: Not the desires of those who do not know
then: Ibn Kathir says this tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}follow what was revealed to you from your Lord{/idea}, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know. It comes right after the warning about splitting.
now: Everyone on your timeline has an opinion on how to live, what to want, what to drop. {trap}Their loudness is not knowledge.{/trap} You already have a way. Walk it.
old: I should shape my life around what most people think is right.
new: I have been given a clear way. Others' desires are not a guide.
try: Mute one account today that keeps pulling you away from your values.

title: Allah is the protector of the mindful.
subtitle: Wrongdoers back each other, and it fails
then: Ibn Kathir asks what the loyalty of wrongdoers to each other will give them: {trap}only more loss and ruin{/trap}. But {reward}Allah is the Protector of those who have taqwa{/reward}, and He brings them out of darkness into light.
now: The group at work that covers for each other's shortcuts. It feels safe to be inside it. {reward}Allah's protection does not depend on being in any crowd.{/reward}
old: I am safest when I am inside the strong group.
new: The One who protects the mindful is the only backing that holds.
try: Do the right thing in one small situation today even if the group does otherwise.

title: Insight for people, and mercy for the certain.
subtitle: The Quran as a way of seeing
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to the Quran: {idea}a clear insight and evidence for mankind{/idea}, and {reward}a guidance and a mercy for people of certainty{/reward}. Basa'ir means things that help you see.
now: New glasses: suddenly the street signs are sharp and you realise how blurry life was. {idea}The Quran is meant to work like that.{/idea} Not just read, but looked through.
old: The Quran is something I read, then return to my day.
new: The Quran is a lens to see my day through.
try: Carry one verse in mind today and look at one situation through it.

title: Do the wrongdoers think they will be treated alike?
subtitle: Good and evil are never equal
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the believers and the disbelievers are never equal{/idea}, in this life or the next. Thinking otherwise is a bad thought about Allah's justice. He reports that Tamim ad-Dari once {reward}stood in night prayer until morning reciting only this verse{/reward}.
now: You watch someone cheat their way up at work and do fine. You wonder if being honest was pointless. {idea}The verse says it was never the same, and it will not end the same.{/idea}
old: In the end, the honest and the cheaters end up in the same place.
new: Allah's justice will never treat the doer of good like the doer of evil.
try: Recite this verse slowly once tonight, the way Tamim ad-Dari did, and let it sink in.

title: Created in truth, so each soul gets its due.
subtitle: Justice is built into creation
then: Ibn Kathir explains created with truth as {idea}created in justice{/idea}, so that each person is recompensed for what he earned, and {reward}they will not be wronged{/reward}. It answers the false assumption of the verse before.
now: You were passed over for a promotion you earned. The unfairness sits in your chest. {reward}Nothing you did is lost from the record.{/reward} Full justice is coming.
old: Some of my efforts will just disappear unseen.
new: Creation was built on justice. Every soul gets exactly its due.
try: Think of one unfairness you carry and say: Allah, You are the Just, I trust You with it.

title: Have you seen one who made his desire his god?
subtitle: When wanting becomes the one who commands
then: Ibn Kathir describes one who {trap}abides by his lust: whatever it portrays as good he does, whatever it portrays as evil he leaves{/trap}. Allah left him astray after knowledge reached him, so he no longer hears, understands or sees what would help him.
now: You skip the prayer because you are not in the mood. You buy it because you want it. You say it because it feels good to say. {trap}Who is actually giving the orders?{/trap}
old: Following my feelings is just being true to myself.
new: If my desire always decides, it has become my god.
try: Today, do one good thing you do not feel like doing, just because Allah wants it.

title: Only time destroys us, they said, without knowledge.
subtitle: Blaming time for what Allah decrees
then: Ibn Kathir says this was the creed of those who denied resurrection: {trap}only this life, and time destroys us{/trap}. They had no knowledge, only guesses. He cites the hadith: do not curse time, for {idea}Allah turns the night and day{/idea}. In Jahiliyyah people blamed time for every disaster.
now: "This year has been cursed." "These are terrible times." You type it after a bad week. {idea}Time does nothing on its own. Every day is turned by Allah.{/idea}
old: Bad times just happen, and time is cruel.
new: Time is not my enemy. Allah turns the days, and I turn to Him.
try: The next time you want to say this year is cursed, say: Allah, make what remains good.

title: Their only argument: bring back our fathers.
subtitle: Clear verses met with one demand

row.title: a reflection
sub: who made me the first time

then: Ibn Kathir says when {idea}the truth is made plain to them{/idea}, that Allah can raise bodies after they decay, {trap}their only argument is: bring back our fathers{/trap}. The same demand was made in the surah before, at 44:36.
now: When a conversation about faith gets uncomfortable, you reach for one stock line you have used for years. {trap}A single comeback is not an answer.{/trap}
old: I have a good counterargument, so I do not need to think further.
new: When my only reply is a demand, I have stopped actually thinking.
try: Write your biggest objection about faith and then look up one real answer to it.

title: He gives you life, then death, then gathers you.
subtitle: The One who started it can repeat it
then: Ibn Kathir says you are witnesses that {idea}He brings you to existence after non-existence{/idea}. So {idea}He who began creation can bring it back{/idea}, and that is easier for Him. The raising is on the Day of Resurrection, not in this life.
now: You hold a newborn and cannot believe a person came from nothing. {idea}That same power is what raises the dead.{/idea} The first creation is the proof of the second.
old: Coming back to life after death is too hard to believe.
new: If He made me from nothing, bringing me back is easier.
try: Look at an old photo of yourself as a baby and reflect on who gave you that first life.

title: When the Hour comes, the followers of falsehood lose.
subtitle: The King of heaven and earth
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}the King and Owner of the heavens and earth{/idea}, the only Ruler now and in the Hereafter. On the Day, {trap}those who rejected the clear proofs will lose{/trap}.
now: You won the argument by twisting a fact. You closed the sale with a small lie. It feels like a win. {trap}Every win built on falsehood is a loss held over.{/trap}
old: Whoever comes out on top now is the winner.
new: The only win that lasts is one built on truth.
try: Correct one exaggeration or false impression you gave someone recently.

title: Every nation on its knees, called to its record.
subtitle: The verse that names the surah
then: This is the verse that gives al-Jathiyah its name. Ibn Kathir says every nation will be {trap}kneeling, fearful of the tremendous events{/trap}. It was said even Ibrahim and Isa will say, myself, myself. {idea}Each nation is called to its record{/idea} and repaid for what it did.
now: Your exam results land in an envelope with your name on it. No one else's work is inside. {idea}One day a record will be handed to you, with only your deeds in it.{/idea}
old: What people think of me says how I am doing.
new: What counts is the record of what I did, called out by name.
try: Tonight, before sleep, review your day honestly for one minute, as if reading your record.

title: Our record speaks of you with truth.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing deleted
then: Ibn Kathir says the record {idea}contains all your actions, without addition or deletion{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said the angels' records are compared with what was written beforehand, and {idea}not a single letter was added or deleted{/idea}.
now: You tell the story of the argument and you come out looking reasonable. Everyone does. {idea}The record does not take your version. It speaks for itself.{/idea}
old: How I explain my actions is how they will be judged.
new: My record speaks the truth about me, with no spin.
try: Think of one story you tell where you are the hero, and admit your part honestly to yourself.

title: Believers who did good enter His mercy.
subtitle: Paradise called by its other name
then: Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}those whose hearts believed and whose limbs did good deeds{/idea}, sincerely. Their Lord admits them into His mercy, and that is Paradise. He cites: Allah said to Paradise, {reward}you are My mercy{/reward}.
now: You hope to get in someday, and you picture gardens. {reward}This verse gives Paradise another name: His mercy.{/reward} Believing with your heart and acting with your hands is how you walk toward it.
old: Paradise is a reward I am working off a list for.
new: Paradise is His mercy, and faith with good deeds is the way in.
try: Match one belief you hold with one act today: if you believe in charity, give something.

title: Were My verses not recited to you?
subtitle: Pride that turned away after hearing
then: The question on the Day is not whether they knew. Ibn Kathir explains it as: {reward}were not the verses of the Most Merciful recited to you?{/reward} But {trap}you did not follow them out of pride{/trap} and turned away on hearing them.
now: The app on your phone has the whole Quran. The masjid is ten minutes away. {idea}On the Day, "I did not know" will be a hard thing to say.{/idea}
old: I will be excused because I did not really know.
new: I have heard enough. The question is whether I follow it.
try: Act today on one thing from the Quran that you already know but have been avoiding.

title: We only guess, they said. We are not sure.
subtitle: Uncertainty used as a shelter
then: When believers told them the Hour is certain, Ibn Kathir says they answered: {trap}we only remotely think it might come{/trap}, we are not sure of it. The guess gave them permission to do nothing.
now: "Who knows what happens after death?" It sounds open minded. Then you notice it is always said when you would rather not change something. {trap}Not sure can be a comfortable place to hide.{/trap}
old: Since no one can be sure, I do not need to prepare.
new: Saying I am not sure can be a way of avoiding what I should do.
try: Ask yourself honestly: is there something I avoid because I tell myself I am not sure?

title: The evil they did will show itself to them.
subtitle: What was mocked surrounds them
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}the repercussions of their evil deeds will become apparent to them{/trap}, and what they mocked, the coming punishment, will surround them from all directions. What was hidden in this life is shown.
now: The browser history you cleared. The message you deleted. You feel it is gone. {idea}The verse says deeds surface. Tawbah is how you meet them before they meet you.{/idea}
old: What I did long ago is over and done.
new: Deeds do not vanish. Repenting now changes how they meet me.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one specific thing you have never asked forgiveness for.

title: Today We forget you, as you forgot this Day.
subtitle: Forgetting the meeting has a cost
then: Ibn Kathir says they forgot the meeting and {trap}did not work for it{/trap}. He cites a hadith: Allah will ask a servant, did I not give you a spouse, honour you, give you means? Then: {trap}did you think you would meet Me?{/trap} No. Then today I forget you as you forgot Me.
now: You remember every bill date, every birthday, every login. {idea}The one appointment you never prepare for is the meeting with Allah.{/idea} Remembering it now is the whole point of the verse.
old: I am too busy right now to think about meeting Allah.
new: Remembering the meeting now is what keeps me from being forgotten then.
try: Set one daily reminder on your phone that says: you will meet Allah.

title: You mocked His verses and this life fooled you.
subtitle: The two causes, named plainly
then: Ibn Kathir says the cause was that {trap}they mocked Allah's proofs{/trap} and made jokes of them, and {trap}this life fooled them{/trap}. On that Day they are not taken out, and no apology is asked of them.
now: Life is full: deadlines, holidays, renovations, a new show every week. {trap}It is easy to be fooled into thinking this is everything.{/trap} The verse names the trick so you can see it.
old: This life is busy, but it is the main event.
new: This life can fool me. The real chance is now, while I am in it.
try: Give ten minutes today that you would spend on entertainment to something for your akhirah.

title: All praise to the Lord of heavens, earth and all worlds.
subtitle: The surah closes with praise
then: Ibn Kathir notes that after Allah mentioned His judgement for believers and disbelievers, He said: {idea}all praise is due to Allah{/idea}, Owner of the heavens, the earth and all in them. The surah of signs and judgement ends in praise.
now: You finish a heavy chapter and close the app with a tight chest. {idea}Pause and say alhamdulillah.{/idea} The same Lord who judges is the One who deserves every praise.
old: Verses about judgement leave me only anxious.
new: His judgement is just, and that itself is a reason to praise Him.
try: Say alhamdulillahi rabbil alamin slowly three times after you finish reading today.

title: His is the grandeur in the heavens and earth.
subtitle: Pride is His garment alone

row.title: His alone
sub: I am in need of Him

then: Mujahid said grandeur here means kingship. Ibn Kathir says {idea}everything and everyone is in complete need of Him{/idea}. He cites the hadith: {trap}glory is My robe and pride is My garment; whoever rivals Me for either{/trap} is warned of the Fire.
now: The moment you feel too important to apologise, to wait in line, to be corrected. {trap}That is reaching for a garment that is not yours.{/trap} The surah that began with signs ends by putting you in your place, gently.
old: A bit of pride is just healthy self-respect.
new: Grandeur belongs to Allah. My dignity is in being His servant.
try: Do one thing today that quietly lowers your pride, like apologising first.
